extracted.intended_audience: readers and commenters on The A.V. Club website
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and expectations for participating in The A.V. Club's online comments: acceptable tone, disallowed behaviors, reporting instructions, and examples of acceptable vs. unacceptable remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall tone — intelligence and wit
rubrics_metrics.description: We strive to cover pop culture with intelligence and wit, and we assume that’s what brought you here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect comments to follow that spirit: informed, witty discussion rather than simple abuse or obscenity. The site takes the 'club' aspect seriously — it’s your site too.

rubrics_metrics.name: No abusive/offensive/obscene posts
rubrics_metrics.description: Abusive/offensive/obscene posts simply don’t contribute to the site's goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid posts that are purely aggressive or insulting with no point. Example of unacceptable: 'You’re a dick!' Example of acceptable (still insulting but with a point): 'Only a dick would watch Con Air six times in a row!' Better (witty critique): 'You watched Con Air six times?! You should’ve taken IQ tests before and after to see how it affected you.'

rubrics_metrics.name: No flagrant personal attacks on other commentators, staffers, or subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Flagrant attacks — particularly aggressive, insulting posts with no other point to make — are unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique work, not people. If your comment is only an attack with no substantive argument, it may be removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: No offensive commentary on interview/review subjects (ad hominem/sexualized remarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Offensive commentary on interview/review subjects, including ad hominem thoughts on how they look, how they might smell, and exactly what you’d like to do to them in bed, is unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may criticize someone’s work, but attacking their appearance or making explicit sexual comments is childish and inappropriate. The policy frames this as behavior that would get you 'uninvited' from a real-world party.

rubrics_metrics.name: No racist, homophobic, or sexist remarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Racist, homophobic, or sexist remarks are explicitly disallowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don’t assume everyone understands your sarcasm, irony, or over-the-top tone; attack comments do not get a free pass because the author claims they 'didn’t really mean it.'

rubrics_metrics.name: No blatant trolling
rubrics_metrics.description: Blatant trolling is listed as unacceptable behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not post intentionally inflammatory content meant solely to provoke or derail discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: No blatant self-promotion or plugs for your own website
rubrics_metrics.description: Blatant plugs for your own website are unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using the comments as advertising or referral space for your own projects or sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: No offensive images or GIFs
rubrics_metrics.description: Offensive images or GIFs are specifically prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep multimedia contributions within the same standards as text: avoid material that is insulting, obscene, or otherwise offensive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community responsibility — report unacceptable behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: The site cannot be everywhere at once; readers can help maintain quality by reporting offenders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you see someone behaving offensively in the comments, contact us (link provided). Community reporting helps enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: General behavioral exhortation — be passionate but be kind
rubrics_metrics.description: Be passionate, but be kind. Learn from each other. And remember there is an actual human being on the other end of the line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the guiding interpersonal standard for participation: vigorous debate is allowed, but maintain civility and empathy.
